rules.sentence: The gold standard for diagnosing SEA is magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which has almost completely replaced myelography.
MRI is as sensitive and specific as CT-myelography.[18]
For patients with IEA, CT or MRI can be used, with the latter providing more detailed information.

The management usually comprises decompressive surgery and drainage of the abscess (considered the gold standard in most circumstances), eradication of the primary underlying infectious focus (if detectable), and parenteral antibiotic therapy to target likely etiologic agents, eg, coagulase-negative staphylococci, streptococci, and gram-negative rods.
